body:
| Peter, can I share a photo with you? [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/90479015/490646146/-972566244?amount=10&refcode=RTFC_20240808_EMSPL_E1_T0_AC&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NjE2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhY2Q0YzFmMS1kOTU1LWVmMTEtOTkxYS02MDQ1YmRkYmZjNGIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=pG3sKo1dPlRFvOAO2cWli_iXWllqrZZ9jo6iARdNiqk=) That young guy, missing his two front teeth with a curious look in his eye? Yup, that’s me!

And if you had told him that nowadays, I’d be running for the U.S. Senate from the great state of California, he would no doubt be very pleased — but genuinely shocked.

You see, growing up, I was fascinated by history and politics.

Sitting around the dinner table at night, we’d talk about the news of the day or the history book my father was reading at the moment.

The conversation was always dynamic — my dad comes from a long line of Democrats, and my mom from a long line of Republicans (in fact, her father was a Republican County chairman at one point, so you can imagine the discourse at larger family gatherings!).

Back then, Democrats and Republicans disagreed with each other about plenty of issues, but you could disagree without being disagreeable.

What changed? Many things. How we get our information. Cable news. Algorithms set to exploit fear and anger.

When I started in politics, Democrats and Republicans would work together to get things done. They often disagreed — _strongly_ — but they put the best interests of the American people first and found areas where they could agree.

**But those days feel long gone now.** We have seen a seismic shift in the last few years — since a charlatan celebrity and reality TV host who called disabled veterans “suckers” and “losers,” denigrated our immigrant communities, and railed on about “fake news” was elected President of the United States.

I’ve never been one to back down from the bullies — so amidst these attempts to dismantle our democracy, I did my duty and called him out and held him to account. I took on this work not because it was easy, but because it needed to be done.

**And for taking on this work, I’ve become Trump’s favorite boogeyman and enemy.**

The little boy in the picture at the beginning of this email never would have imagined bearing the brunt of insults from a U.S. President and his cronies in Congress and the far-right media.

But if standing up for our democracy, for our rights and freedoms, and for our Constitution has earned me the enmity of Trump and the MAGA movement, then that’s a badge of honor I will wear proudly every day.

[These are the fights I’m going to take on in the U.S. Senate — where many of Trump’s chief enablers reside. Which is why Trump is doing everything he can to stop me from winning. clean_body: | Peter, can I share a photo with you? = That young guy, missing his two front teeth with a curious look in his eye? Yup, that’s me! And if you had told him that nowadays, I’d be running for the U.S. Senate from the great state of California, he would no doubt be very pleased — but genuinely shocked. You see, growing up, I was fascinated by history and politics. Sitting around the dinner table at night, we’d talk about the news of the day or the history book my father was reading at the moment. The conversation was always dynamic — my dad comes from a long line of Democrats, and my mom from a long line of Republicans (in fact, her father was a Republican County chairman at one point, so you can imagine the discourse at larger family gatherings!). Back then, Democrats and Republicans disagreed with each other about plenty of issues, but you could disagree without being disagreeable. What changed? Many things. How we get our information. Cable news. Algorithms set to exploit fear and anger. When I started in politics, Democrats and Republicans would work together to get things done. They often disagreed — strongly — but they put the best interests of the American people first and found areas where they could agree. But those days feel long gone now. We have seen a seismic shift in the last few years — since a charlatan celebrity and reality TV host who called disabled veterans “suckers” and “losers,” denigrated our immigrant communities, and railed on about “fake news” was elected President of the United States. I’ve never been one to back down from the bullies — so amidst these attempts to dismantle our democracy, I did my duty and called him out and held him to account. I took on this work not because it was easy, but because it needed to be done. And for taking on this work, I’ve become Trump’s favorite boogeyman and enemy. The little boy in the picture at the beginning of this email never would have imagined bearing the brunt of insults from a U.S. President and his cronies in Congress and the far-right media. But if standing up for our democracy, for our rights and freedoms, and for our Constitution has earned me the enmity of Trump and the MAGA movement, then that’s a badge of honor I will wear proudly every day. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between Adam Schiff and Ritchie Torres will go through immediately: | = = = Many of the most important fights for the future of our democracy will be waged in the U.S. Senate in the years to come. Friends --
While I know our campaign has sent a lot of emails because of this week's primary, where I offically became the Democratic nominee for U.S Senate in Michigan, I want to take a few minutes to tell you about my decision to run for Senate in the first place, and why your support is so important in our success.
The truth is, we all know America is _going through something_ right now. We seem to be living from crisis to crisis. But there are certain things that should be really simple:
Like living a middle-class life in the state that invented the middle class.
Like making things in America so that we’re in control of our own economic security.
Like protecting our children from the things that are _truly_ harming them.
And preserving our rights and our democracy so that our kids can live their version of the American dream.
**I’m running for Senate because I believe that we need a new generation of leaders that thinks differently, works harder, and never forgets the mission of public service.**
But my decision to run for Senate is also deeply personal to me, and it's related to what motivated me to first run for the House in 2018.
It's about my mom, Judy. She was diagnosed with stage IV ovarian cancer in 2009 — and didn't have health insurance at the time. She had let it lapse after the insurance companies had gouged her for years because she happened to have a pre-existing condition. She passed away in 2011, but that experience — of desperately trying to get her care at the same moment we were filling out bankruptcy paperwork — fueled me to run. I remember the exact moment that made me run: when the then-GOP controlled House of Representatives, the body I now serve in, voted to repeal those protections for people with pre-existing conditions.
Seven years later, the Republican leaders, fueled by the extreme wing of the party, are continuing the march to repeal things that the average Americans want. They want to privatize Social Security and Medicare, repeal drug price protections like allowing Medicare to negotiate, then there’s the rights they’re obsessed with repealing: a woman’s right to choose, voting rights, and any possible gun safety legislation.
By winning this Senate seat, we’ll help ensure that Democrats retain the (slight!) majority and can pass legislation that expands access to healthcare. Not the obsession with taking things away.
To be upfront: **Winning this race is going to take a lot of resources. A crazy amount. And we have to do it without raising a single dollar from corporate PACs.**
[**That is why I would love it if you would consider donating $3 or whatever you can to my campaign before our as we're now in the final sprint of this campaign.](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-aug24._YMjeK&refcode=em240808-3-900k&t=3&akid=1747%2E135344%2EPI-O1O)**

body:
Since JD Vance has a problem with women being childless, you would assume he wants to make it easier for parents to raise families.

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2302%2E4032634%2EHTeRIv)
---
I don’t have to tell you why JD Vance’s past comments about “childless cat ladies running the country” are sexist and out-of-touch. But because he’s got a problem with women being childless, you would assume that he must be interested in making it easier for parents to raise families, right? Maybe just a little? Well, he recently voted against a bill in Congress that would protect access to IVF care federally. He has voted against extending the child tax credit, which reduced child poverty by about 30 percent in less than one year. And in the past, he has described the idea of universal child care as class warfare on the working class — which doesn’t make any sense at all. If that’s not rich enough, when recently given the chance to clarify his comments about childless cat ladies, he said, “This is about criticizing the Democratic Party for becoming anti-family and anti-child.” Give me a break. We’re not buying that. [**I could go on and on about how Republicans don’t do anything to _actually_ support families. I’m not willing to accept any of this charade — and I’m fighting my heart out to pass plans that actually help working families. If you’re with me, please pitch in $28 or anything you can so I can keep fighting in the Senate.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/2542?amount=28&t=8&akid=2302%2E4032634%2EHTeRIv)

Democrats are the ones fighting for access to reproductive care, paid family leave, affordable child care, strong public schools for every family, good-paying jobs that leave parents with time to see their kids, and a government that works for every family. Meanwhile if it were up to JD Vance, Trump, and the Republican Party: Without access to contraceptives or safe abortion care, more people are forced to give birth — sometimes in situations that threaten their lives — on a politician’s terms instead of their own. That’s anti-family. That’s anti-child. Without affordable child care measures, more parents — especially moms — are forced to give up their careers because the monthly costs are more than their monthly salary. That’s anti-family. That’s anti-child. Without paid family leave, more parents are forced to make impossible choices between going to work that day so they can buy groceries or staying home so they can take care of a sick child. That’s anti-family. That’s anti-child. As a die-hard defender of our Right to Bear Arms, I encouraged my staff to open carry at work. Liberals hated me for it.
...But it made me a Congresswoman instead.

| |

---
| | | My restaurant almost landed me in jail - but it made me a Congresswoman instead.

My name is Lauren Boebert. Before serving in Congress, I was serving hungry Coloradans as the owner of Shooters Grill in Rifle, Colorado. As a die-hard defender of our Right to Bear Arms, I encouraged my staff to open carry at work. Liberals hated me for it.

A few years later, I made even more headlines when I defied power hungry politicians during COVID and opened up my restaurant anyway. **They sued me. They tried to close my doors forever. And they made me an enemy of the state.**

_But I 'm a mama bear of 4 boys - it takes a LOT more than a few empty suits to scare me!_

I'm tough. And now that I'm in Congress, I'm not afraid to ruffle some feathers and speak my mind. I'll never stop fighting for President Trump, my faith, my country, or our God-given rights.

Unfortunately, defeating Kamala Harris, defending our freedoms, and saving our country will be EXPENSIVE. Biden handed over his 91 million dollar warchest on day one AND the Democrat Machine raised another 200 million bucks when Kamala was coronated. _**[That's why I'm teaming up with Majority Leader Steve Scalise to raise a million dollars from this email alone to help.](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=ccd6df9670f9424586272602cf2e8b81&_e=ArAL0owoTn6PbuMHyeYNUcQM9h26ZBQi6hrGKonAHGqSEPhYrUv4gcgUxqB288hz59OjbY0-RfZqExnX5I1ykm5TAjRx7RvQGgqekwelw6rLiW4dvTAEHvY2fovoMp2mnqZltVzgo3JEP-P5DvD1E5u8jVyyRRohytwQxBbHR560lIP3trVgtjKOlWhkFhPKUzZXG14ydjDZeeRKCKa4ijS1jcR1UGWZ1B8Hg7eaHDA2NRKr7rQX7mSE7MX6uyYPwtLQIu42VfjoIPbdPnf4cOW0kGyf8Rn1doy2w9HLZHyi5voy_w91Y6GvlY4RVMvZzVYF4IooHZMQjXbqD0jr3sM5EUzbldrAo7033KgGhH7Ex4QnUHA08HBk-UNFF85ZNgxcrgLRbSRtKE0SxTXcTw%3D%3D "That’s why I’m teaming up with Majority Leader Steve Scalise to raise a million dollars from this email alone to help. body:
Together, we built a powerful movement and united folks across the District, from Neah Bay to Commencement Bay.

| Peter,

I wanted to express my deepest thanks for your incredible support throughout this campaign. Your dedication and hard work have meant the world to me.

While this race didn’t turn out as planned, our fight for progress in the face of unprecedented challenges is far from over. The issues we’ve championed — from climate change and education to workforce development and childcare — remain critical.

Together, we built a powerful movement and united folks across the District, from Neah Bay to Commencement Bay, behind our message of lowering costs, creating economic opportunity, addressing our housing needs, protecting our freedoms, and addressing the climate crisis. I’m especially grateful to the over 40 unions, firefighters and first responders, and 17 Tribes that stood with me in this race.

As we look ahead to November, it’s crucial that we stay engaged and keep pushing forward. I’ve called Senator Randall to congratulate her on her historic primary win, and it is time for all of us to work harder than ever so we can flip the House, defeat Donald Trump, and defend our democracy.

Thank you for standing with me. Together, we will keep working to make a difference.

With sincere appreciation,

Hilary Franz
---
